subject: english
question:
Directions: Each of the following questions has underlined idioms/phrases. Each sentence is followed by four options. Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase.

As the actors gathered backstage, the director shouted, “**__Break a leg__**, everyone!” before they took the stage for their opening night performance.

options.text: To get a good night's sleep

solution:
The correct answer is **"To wish someone good luck."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Break a leg"** is a common idiom used in the theatre industry to wish someone good luck before a performance. (प्रदर्शन से पहले किसी को शुभकामनाएं देना)

 
 
• **Example**: *Danny's family told him to **“break a leg”**__ right before he went up on stage.*
 
 
 
• The origin of the phrase is uncertain, but it is believed to have originated as a way to ward off bad luck by wishing for the opposite to happen.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.
